answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The haven multiplier is published, charged in tide, and beacon lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1674 identities would post 2746 proofs and burn roughly 12 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
